question: On a hydraulic test rig, the base setting x of a ram is the smaller of the two values that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 30 = 0. The rig controller adds 3 to that setting, multiplies the result by 9, and then subtracts 8 to obtain the acceleration, in m/s^2, commanded for the sled clamped to the ram. The sled has a mass of 53000 grams. The rig runs 9 identical rams in parallel, each pushing an identical sled with that same acceleration. What is the total thrust, in N, delivered by all 9 rams together?

A robotics lab keeps 9 interchangeable battery packs and counts every way of choosing 2 of them to fit into a test cart. The technician sets the cart's launch speed, in m/s, to that count minus 14. The cart has a mass of 10000 grams. The energy of motion the cart carries at launch is recorded in kJ, and a 2 kJ allowance for energy already stored in its flywheel is subtracted from that reading to give the net launch figure. What net launch figure, in kJ, is recorded?

The number a crane operator must log, in kN, is a corrected total: start from 8 times the drive force on one trolley (with that force expressed in kN), subtract 22 kN of cable relief, then add 30 kN of standing counterweight load. The trolley has a mass of 22 kg and rides a boom that is 14 m long. Its acceleration, in m/s^2, is the larger of the two values x for which x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0, and the drive force is exactly what produces that acceleration. What corrected total, in kN, goes in the log?

The quantity the structural team wants, in N, is the grand total load on a launch platform: 5 identical bays, each carrying 9 identical racks, each rack holding 5 identical thrusters, every thruster contributing the same force. Each thruster pushes a 68 kg test mass along a frictionless guide. The acceleration it gives that mass, in m/s^2, is 18 more than the largest whole number that divides both 98 and 343 exactly. What is the grand total load on the platform, in N?

A maglev test sled runs along a straight track, and its position in metres after t seconds is s(t) = 4t^3 - 1t^2. An engineer takes the sled's acceleration at t = 3 s, subtracts 1, and uses the result, in m/s, as the target speed of a second, heavier sled of mass 43 kg that runs on a parallel track kept at 20 degrees C. The heavier sled's energy of motion at that target speed, plus 8 J stored in its brake spring, is the energy one run deposits in the end buffer. The buffer absorbs 6 such runs before it is inspected. How much energy, in J, does the buffer absorb between inspections?

The value a ride-safety inspector wants, in J, is the energy of motion of a 50 kg cart at its top speed plus an 8 J contribution from its spring-loaded restraint bar. The top speed in m/s is 4 times a base figure, and the base figure is 14 less than the area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 3x between x = 1 and x = 3. The cart runs on a loop track 85 m long. What value, in J, does the inspector record?

On a rail-brake test bench, two timing gears have 54 and 396 teeth, and the controller sets a base number equal to the largest number of teeth that divides both counts exactly. It adds 17 to that base number and then subtracts 18 to obtain the sled's commanded acceleration in m/s^2. The sled has a mass of 59000 grams. The drive supplies exactly the force needed for that acceleration, while the rail brake applies 26 kN in the opposite direction. Taking the drive direction as positive, what is the net force on the sled, in kN?

The final entry on a catapult test sheet is the total launch load in kN: the force needed to accelerate the carriage, plus 12 N of guide-rail friction. The carriage has a mass of 38000 grams. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is 4 less than a base figure, and the base figure is 4 times the sum of 9 and 7. What is the total launch load, in kN?

A warehouse sorting line uses two chain sprockets with 222 and 346 links per revolution, and the control software takes the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly as a base setting. It multiplies the base setting by 3 and then by 4 to get the acceleration, in m/s^2, given to each parcel tote. Each tote has a mass of 129 kg and slides on a frictionless bed. The line runs 11 totes at once, each pushed by its own actuator with that same acceleration. What is the combined force, in N, that the 11 actuators exert?

A rescue drone of mass 56000 grams is flight-tested at a coastal base. Its cruise speed in m/s is fixed by a calibration rule: take the area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 4x between x = 2 and x = 4, subtract 14, then add 7. Four identical drones fly at that cruise speed in formation. Find the total energy of motion of the formation, in kJ.

A parcel-launching test rig at a logistics lab fires a 27000 gram dummy package along a rail. The package's release speed in m/s equals the area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 6x between x = 1 and x = 3. Its energy of motion at release is recorded in kJ. The rig then adds 4 kJ of stored spring energy to that reading and subtracts 11 kJ absorbed by the catch net to get the net figure for the report. What net figure, in kJ, appears in the report?

A shuttle on an automated car-park lift has a mass of 172 kg and travels a vertical run of 18 m. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is 3 more than the smaller of the two values x that satisfy x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0. The motor supplies the force needed for that acceleration plus 24 N of guide friction. The lift runs 9 such shuttles simultaneously, each with its own motor, and a counterbalance relieves 16 N of the combined motor load. What net force, in N, do the motors supply together after the counterbalance relief?

The figure a plant manager wants, in kN, is the combined net load from 4 identical conveyor sections, each section carrying 7 identical carriers, each carrier producing the same net force. The net force per carrier is the drive force minus 11 N of belt friction. Each carrier has a mass of 48 kg and a bed 1.2 m long. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is the smaller of the two values x that satisfy x^2 - 7x + 6 = 0, and the drive force is exactly what produces that acceleration. What combined net load, in kN, does the manager record?

A stamping press at a metal shop drives a ram of mass 196 kg through a stroke of 0.35 m. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is set to the sum of the terms 2k - 1 for every whole number k from 1 to 6. The press has 10 identical rams, each driven with the force that produces that acceleration. The frame also bears a constant 19 N from the guide springs on top of the rams' combined force. The shop runs 11 identical presses, and the foundation must carry the frame load from all of them. What total load, in N, does the foundation carry?

The figure a materials lab wants, in kJ, is 3 times the per-cycle energy tally of a test rig. The per-cycle tally is the energy of motion of a 9000 gram slider, expressed in kJ, plus 21 kJ of heater energy, plus a further 6 kJ of pump energy. The slider's speed in m/s is the largest whole number that divides both 163 and 87 exactly. What figure, in kJ, does the lab report?

A luggage-conveyor test cart of mass 108000 grams runs on a level bed. Its acceleration in m/s^2 is 9 times the larger of the two values x that satisfy x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0. The force that produces that acceleration is shared: a helper spring contributes 28 N of it and the motor provides the rest, which the plant expresses in kN. Three such carts run side by side under identical conditions. What is the total motor force on the 3 carts, in kN?

A battery-powered luggage tug of mass 47 kg is tested on a straight lane 30 m long. Its test speed in m/s equals the area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 3x between x = 0 and x = 2. For each run the logger takes the tug's energy of motion at that speed, in kJ, and subtracts the 3 kJ drawn from the battery to reach it, recording the difference as the run's energy balance (negative means a deficit). The test consists of 6 identical runs. What is the total energy balance over the 6 runs, in kJ?

The value a rig technician wants, in N, is the total load on a winch mount: the cable pull, plus 28 N of sheave friction, plus 20 N of guide drag, plus 27 N from a tensioning spring. The cable pull is the force required to accelerate a 157 kg carriage along a level rail 40 m long. The carriage's acceleration in m/s^2 equals the area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 0x between x = 1 and x = 3. What total load, in N, does the technician record?

A lab bench holds two encoder discs with 398 and 144 slots, and the bench controller takes the largest whole number that divides both slot counts exactly, then multiplies it by 4 to set the launch speed, in m/s, of a 3 kg test puck. The puck's energy of motion at launch is logged in kJ. The logger adds 6 kJ for the energy held in the launch capacitor and then 11 kJ for the bench heater's contribution. What final figure, in kJ, does the logger show?

An airport baggage tractor tows a cart of mass 177 kg across an apron 60 m wide. The cart's acceleration in m/s^2 is the smaller of the two values x that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 30 = 0. The hitch must transmit the force that produces that acceleration plus 17 N of rolling drag, and the tractor's gauge reads that hitch force in kN. A train of 8 identical carts, each on its own hitch under identical conditions, is towed at once. What total hitch force, in kN, does the gauge report?

The number a safety officer needs, in J, is the total impact energy on a barrier plus 14 J stored in the barrier's pads. The impact energy is delivered by 5 identical waves of 10 identical carts each, every cart hitting the barrier with the same energy of motion. Each cart has a mass of 42 kg and a track width of 0.9 m. The carts' speed in m/s is the largest whole number that divides both 50 and 278 exactly. What number, in J, does the safety officer record?

The figure a workshop wants, in kJ (negative meaning a net loss), is the energy balance of a test: the gross energy captured, expressed in kJ, minus 6 kJ consumed by the test motor. The gross energy captured is 8 identical sled impacts plus 27 J released by a latch spring, where each impact deposits the sled's full energy of motion. The sled has a mass of 26000 grams and rides a track 5 m long. Its speed in m/s is the larger of the two values x that satisfy x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0. What energy balance, in kJ, does the workshop record?

A rail-mounted camera dolly's position along a straight track, in metres, is s(t) = 4t^3 - 2t^2 with t in seconds. A technician takes the dolly's acceleration at t = 3 s, adds 5, then subtracts 25, and uses the result as the launch speed, in m/s, of a 54000 gram test sled on a nearby lab bench that is 2.4 m long. What is the sled's energy of motion at that launch speed, in kJ?

The figure a stadium engineer wants, in kJ, is the total energy delivered to a crash barrier plus 11 kJ already stored in the barrier's dampers. The delivered energy comes from 3 identical test sessions, each session's energy (expressed in kJ) being 4 identical impacts of a sled, every impact depositing the sled's full energy of motion. The sled has a mass of 53 kg and a height of 1.1 m. Its impact speed in m/s is the sum of all the whole numbers from 1 to 10. What figure, in kJ, does the engineer record?

The final reading a lab bench displays, in J, is a running tally: it starts from a test trolley's energy of motion, adds 27 J from a heater, subtracts 14 J lost to friction, subtracts a further 18 J vented by a fan, and finally adds 19 J from a charging coil. The trolley has a mass of 25000 grams. Its speed in m/s is the largest whole number that divides both 321 and 263 exactly. What final reading, in J, does the bench display?
